name: Sylphus
classification_notes: A vertical-contrast Didone-style design with connected serifs, classed as a display serif for its spiky, headline-oriented character.
summary: An elegant, spiky Didone-style display serif with connected serifs and a Phos blur variant.
description: Sylphus grew out of a rejected logotype design into a vertical-contrast, Didone or Bodonesque display family with connected serifs and unusual details. Alongside the main four-weight set it carries a Phos blurred variant and a single-weight mono cut, with full Greek support and three stylistic sets of alternates.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Sylphus as a vertical contrast axis didonesque or bodonesque design with connected serifs and out-of-the-ordinary details, resulting in an elegant, spiky set of letters.

name: Silkscreen Text
classification_notes: The text-weight, multi-style expansion of Silkscreen's contrasted grotesque letterforms, built for smaller sizes than the original display cut.
summary: The text-optimised expansion of Silkscreen's vintage Greek signage grotesque, with italics and a mono cut.
description: Silkscreen Text expands Atypical's caps-only Silkscreen concept into a full text family with lowercase, italics and a monospaced companion, keeping the contrasted grotesque character inspired by 1950s-60s Greek signage.
foundry_blurb: Atypical present Silkscreen Text as part of the wider Silkscreen family, adding regular, medium, semibold and bold weights with italics and a blurred variant for editorial use.

name: Direct Too
classification_notes: The expanded, multi-weight continuation of Direct's practical grotesque, adding rounded and additional weight options.
summary: An expanded six-style continuation of Direct's practical grotesque, adding a rounded companion.
description: Direct Too extends Atypical's Direct family with six additional weights and styles, plus a Direct Too Rounded companion in three weights, keeping the blend of strict geometry with grotesque and humanist detailing that suits technical documents and information design.
foundry_blurb: Atypical present Direct Too as an expansion of Direct, adding further weights and a rounded companion for technical and information-design use.

name: Atypical Text
classification_notes: A text-weight companion to the studio's Atypical caps grotesque, built for body copy rather than headline use.
summary: A body-text grotesque companion to Atypical's caps-only display face.
description: Atypical Text adapts the studio's caps-only Atypical grotesque into a full-charset text face, aimed at body copy and longer reading rather than headline or branding use.
foundry_blurb: Atypical present Atypical Text as a text-focused companion within the wider Atypical family.

name: Forward
classification_notes: A geometric sans with three edge treatments, Diagonal, Square and Round, classed as sans-serif for its futurist geometric structure.
summary: A geometric sans family with a twist, offered in Diagonal, Square and Round edge treatments across five weights each.
description: Forward was designed for and with boo republic as a geometric type family with a twist, its fifteen fonts split across three style categories, Diagonal, Square and Round, distinguished by their corner and edge treatments, each running Light to Bold.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Forward as a geometric type family with a twist, designed for and with boo republic, featuring geometric futurism with three distinct style variations distinguished by edge treatments.

name: Luxurious
classification_notes: A contrasted serif built for logotypes and packaging at large sizes, its elegance and quirks placing it as a display serif.
summary: An elegant, quirky contrasted serif originally commissioned for an Athens design studio's identity.
description: Luxurious began as an exclusive custom typeface for Another Practice, a design studio in Athens, before joining Atypical's retail catalogue. Described by the studio as luxurious and quirky, it suits logotypes, packaging and titles set large.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Luxurious as an elegant contrasted serif initially designed as an exclusive custom typeface for Another Practice in Athens, suited for logotypes, packaging, titles and small texts in large sizes.

name: Dolce Noir
classification_notes: Grouped by the foundry among its serif and display releases; treated as display given the lack of a stated text-weight role.
summary: A decorative display face from Atypical's 2023 releases, built for titles and short-text settings.
description: Dolce Noir is one of Atypical's 2023 releases, a decorative display face intended for titles and short texts rather than continuous reading, with the studio's usual full Greek character support.
foundry_blurb: Atypical list Dolce Noir among their display releases, available with a downloadable PDF specimen and full Greek support.

name: Oedipus
classification_notes: A personal take on classic Roman capitals with two serif treatments, placing it firmly in the serif category.
summary: A personal take on classic Roman capitals in two variations, Sharp and Soft, with long or short serifs.
description: Oedipus reworks classic Roman capitals into two elegant variations, one with long, sharp serifs and one with shorter, rounded serifs, with a curated set of ligatures and letter combinations plus full Greek support.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Oedipus as a personal take on the classic Roman caps, featuring two elegant variations, one with long, sharp serifs and one with shorter rounded serifs, including Greek character support.

name: Miasma
subcategory: high-contrast text serif with grotesque companion
classification_notes: A high-contrast serif built for both extended text and display, with soft and sharp serif treatments and a sans companion.
summary: A high-contrast serif family for extended text, offered in soft and sharp serif cuts plus a sans-serif companion.
description: Miasma is built for both extended text and large display sizes, with two stylistic approaches, softer Miasma and sharper Miasma Sharp, plus a Miasma Grotesque sans companion. Four weights carry matching italics, and it includes two sets of capital Greek letters, with and without serifs, for polytonic Greek.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Miasma as a high-contrast text typeface designed for both extended text and large display sizes, featuring two stylistic approaches with distinct serif treatments and a grotesque companion.

name: Aegithalos
classification_notes: A narrow, tilted high-contrast display face named for a bird, built for titles and short texts at large size.
summary: A narrow display face with tilted, flamboyant contrast, named after the long-tailed tit.
description: Aegithalos is a narrow display typeface with a high tilted contrast and a flamboyant but elegant character, named after Aegithalos caudatus, the long-tailed tit found across Europe. It is built for titles and short texts set large, with Latin, Greek and Cyrillic support.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Aegithalos as a narrow display typeface with a high tilted contrast and a flamboyant but elegant character, named after the long-tailed tit bird found across Europe.

name: Charybdis
classification_notes: A sans-serif with deep ink traps and high x-height, tuned for small text and screen use as much as titles.
summary: An eerie, ink-trapped grotesque across five widths, built for a new Greek typographic weird-wave.
description: Charybdis is eerie, weird and mysterious, described by Atypical as part of a search for a new Greek typographic weird-wave. Deep ink traps, high x-height and occasional high contrast run across five widths from Condensed to Expanded plus a variable font, working in both titles and small-size text.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Charybdis as eerie, weird and mysterious, in search of a new Greek typographic weird-wave, with deep ink traps, high x-height, occasional high contrast and a lot of character.

name: Sauvage
classification_notes: A sans and serif pair built around deliberate gender-typographic tension, with the sans cut placed as the primary category.
summary: A queer sans and serif typographic pair challenging conventional gender associations, named after Bertrand Mandico's film.
description: Sauvage is a queer sans and serif typographic pair that challenges conventional gender associations in type design, its name taken from Bertrand Mandico's film Les Garçons Sauvages. Sauvage Moderne and Sauvage Antique (with reversed Greek contrast) include gender and sexuality symbol ligatures.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Sauvage as a queer sans and serif typographic pair that challenges conventional gender associations in typographic design, functioning in both text and display applications.

name: Hypnosis
classification_notes: An experimental face with wavy stems and open diagonal connections, built to unsettle rather than serve as a workhorse text font.
summary: An experimental display face with wavy stems and open diagonal connections, offered in standard and rounded cuts.
description: Hypnosis is designed to heighten concentration and focus through wavy lowercase ascenders and descenders, open diagonal connections and off-balanced individual characters. It comes in standard and Rounded variants, with monospaced numerals throughout.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Hypnosis as designed to heighten your concentration and focus, creating an altered state of typographic consciousness through wavy stems, open diagonal connections and off-balanced characters.

name: Stephen
classification_notes: A low-contrast, condensed bracketed serif in the lineage of ITC Benguiat and Albertus, with a sans companion.
summary: A low-contrast, condensed bracketed serif named for Stephen King, with a sans-serif counterpart.
description: Stephen is a low-contrast, condensed, space-saving text typeface, its name a tribute to Stephen King seen through a condensed, bracketed serif lens. It follows the lineage of ITC Benguiat, Albertus, Friz Quadrata and Alverata, with a Stephen Sans counterpart and italics throughout.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Stephen as a low-contrast, condensed, space-saving text typeface, its name paying tribute to Stephen King and following the lineage of ITC Benguiat, Albertus, Friz Quadrata and Alverata.

name: Meze
classification_notes: Square-proportioned caps lettering copied from a 1920s Athens café sign, built for titles rather than continuous text.
summary: An almost-square vernacular display face copied from 1920s lettering on an Athens café wall.
description: Meze is inspired by lettering on the walls of the Terpsithea café in Athens' Psirri neighbourhood, photographed around 1920. Its almost-square design suits book titles, posters, web headings, logos and wall lettering, with lowercase and Cyrillic added in later updates.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Meze as inspired by lettering found on walls of the Terpsithea café in Psirri, Athens, photographed around 1920, with an almost-square design suitable for titles, posters, web headings, logos and wall lettering.

name: Vs.
classification_notes: An experimental display face offered with an italic companion, placed in display given its limited public description beyond style count.
summary: An experimental display face with an italic companion, distributed individually or as a two-font pack.
description: Vs. is one of Atypical's earlier experimental display releases, offered as a regular and italic pair with the studio's usual broad Greek and Latin character support.
foundry_blurb: Atypical distribute Vs. as a regular and italic pair, sold individually or as the Vs. Pack.

name: Nobilis
classification_notes: A high-contrast sans with soft, rounded edges built for large display and elegant text, the first Atypical release with full Cyrillic.
summary: A high-contrast, softly rounded display sans, the first Atypical typeface with full Cyrillic support.
description: Nobilis balances elegance with sturdiness through an unusual combination of traits, a high-contrast sans-serif with soft, rounded edges for large display sizes and elegant text. It was the first Atypical typeface with complete Cyrillic support, and a lower-contrast Text variation and variable font followed.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Nobilis as a high-contrast sans-serif with soft, rounded edges designed for large display sizes and elegant text, representing the first Atypical typeface with complete Cyrillic support.

name: PhD
classification_notes: A strict condensed geometric sans with mono and rounded companions, built for a technical, futuristic look.
summary: A strict, pseudo-futuristic condensed geometric sans with monospaced and rounded companions.
description: PhD is a rather strict, condensed, geometric pseudo-futuristic typeface built for titles, subheads and short texts wanting a technical look. Five weights are joined by PhD Mono, PhD Rounded and PhD Mono Rounded companions, with a variable font for the mono cut.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe PhD as a rather strict condensed geometric pseudo-futuristic typeface, built to convey a technical, strict look in titles, subheads and short texts.

name: Atypical
classification_notes: A caps-only grotesque built for headlines and logos, originally designed for the studio's own website.
summary: A caps-only grotesque originally built for the studio's own logo and site, with stencil and inline companions.
description: Atypical, the studio's namesake typeface, is a caps-only grotesque sans-serif ideal for headlines, subheads, logos and web design, initially designed for this very website's logo, titles and buttons. Stencil and Inline companions extend the family, alongside a variable weight version.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe their namesake typeface as a caps only grotesque sans serif ideal for headlines, subheads, logos and web design applications, initially designed for the logo, titles and buttons of their own website.

name: Direct
classification_notes: A practical sans blending strict geometry with grotesque and humanist elements, built for technical and information design.
summary: A practical sans blending strict geometry with grotesque and humanist elements for technical documents.
description: Direct blends strict geometry with grotesque and humanist elements, sitting between humanist, geometric and technical sans-serif styles. Suited to technical documents, text and information design, it comes in regular, italic, bold and bold italic, later expanded by Direct Too.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Direct as blending strict geometry with grotesque and humanistic elements, positioned between humanist, geometric and technical sans serif styles for technical documents, text and information design.

name: Monotonous
classification_notes: A monospaced twist on Direct, built for technical documents and applications like posters or packaging.
summary: A monospaced version of Direct with a twist, built for technical documents, posters and packaging.
description: Monotonous takes Direct's practical grotesque structure and fixes it to a monospaced grid, aimed at technical documents or applications such as posters and packaging. It runs to Regular, Bold and Black, each with a matching italic.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Monotonous as a monospaced version of Direct with a twist, designed for technical documents or applications such as posters or packaging.

name: Proportional
classification_notes: A condensed grotesque inspired by proportionally spaced typewriter research, its technical spacing logic keeping it in the sans-serif category.
summary: A condensed grotesque inspired by Alan Bartram's research into proportionally spaced typewriter fonts.
description: Proportional draws on Alan Bartram's research into proportionally spaced typewriter fonts, using fixed spacing values of 80 to 480 units per em for a technical, semi-organic rhythm. Originally made exclusively for backpacker.gr's tenth-anniversary edition, it later gained Cyrillic support.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Proportional as a condensed grotesque typeface inspired by Alan Bartram's research on proportionally spaced typewriter fonts, using fixed spacing values for balanced, semi-organic results.

name: Joy-D
classification_notes: An angled-axis humanist sans with compressed stems and broad-pen-inspired detailing.
summary: A postmodern humanist sans with a slightly angled axis and broad-pen-inspired detailing.
description: Joy-D is a humanist sans with a slightly angled axis, compressed upright stems and low-to-medium contrast, reminiscent of broad-edged pen designs. Light, Light Italic, Regular and Bold cover titles, subheads and body text, with old style numerals included.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Joy-D as a humanist sans with a slightly angled axis, compressed upright stems and low-to-medium contrast, reminiscent of broad-edged pen designs.

name: Luxus
classification_notes: A display face inspired by extreme serif expansion in vintage logotypes, offered in a contrasted serif and a monolinear slab cut.
summary: An elegant, strong display face inspired by the extreme serif expansion of Electrolux and Tecno logos.
description: Luxus is inspired by the extreme serif expansion seen in the Electrolux and Tecno logos, described by Atypical as thoroughly designed, elegant and strong. It comes in a contrasted serif cut, Luxus, and a monolinear slab-serif cut, Luxus Not, originally made for backpacker.gr's tenth-anniversary edition.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Luxus as a thoroughly designed display typeface, elegant and strong at the same time, inspired by the extreme serif expansion seen in Electrolux and Tecno logos.

name: Silkscreen
classification_notes: A caps-only contrasted grotesque inspired by vintage Greek signage, the founding cut of the wider Silkscreen family.
summary: A caps-only contrasted grotesque with a retro touch, inspired by 1950s-60s Greek signage and posters.
description: Silkscreen is a caps-only contrasted grotesque inspired by vintage Greek signage and posters from the 1950s and 60s, built for titles wanting an elegant, retro touch. It has grown into a wider family including Condensed, Display and a Text sub-family with mono and blurred variants.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Silkscreen as a caps-only contrasted grotesque inspired by vintage Greek signage and posters from the 1950s-60s, designed for titles requiring an elegant, retro touch.

name: Burger
classification_notes: An extra-wide display face copied from mid-century Greek commercial signage, built for bold, wide headline use.
summary: An extra-wide display face inspired by old signage found in Thessaloniki, Greece.
description: Burger is an extra-wide typeface inspired by old signage found in Thessaloniki, Greece, created as homage to vintage sign makers and referencing the Takis burger house sign. Originally caps-only, it gained lowercase in 2019, and runs to Regular, Bold and Rounded variants, each with italics.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Burger as an extra wide typeface inspired by old signage found in Thessaloniki, Greece, created as homage to vintage sign makers referencing mid-century commercial lettering.

name: Slab
classification_notes: An experimental humanist, monolinear slab serif offered in multiple slab variations plus sans and high-contrast companions.
summary: A free experimental humanist slab serif with four slab variations plus sans and high-contrast companions.
description: Slab is an experiment on a humanist, monolinear slab-serif design with four different slab variations, primarily intended for display use at large sizes. Three light grades with italics are joined by a sans-serif version, two high-contrast cuts and monospaced serif and sans variants.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Slab as an experiment upon a humanist, monolinear, slab serif design with multiple slab variations, a total of four different slabs, designed primarily for display applications in large text sizes.

name: Friday
classification_notes: A gentle, low-contrast display serif with an exceptionally large x-height, aimed at titles and short luxury-brand text.
summary: A free, gentle display serif with a large x-height and a low-contrast book weight, built for luxury applications.
description: Friday is a gentle and elegant display serif with a vertical axis, an exceptionally large x-height and a low-contrast book weight, working well in titles and short texts and described by the studio as ideal for luxury applications.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Friday as a gentle and elegant design with a vertical axis, exceptionally large x-height and low contrast book weight, working great in titles and short texts and ideal for luxury applications.

name: Marx
classification_notes: A condensed, bold Didone serif with exceptional detail inspired by 1970s Greek book-cover lettering, built for large display sizes.
summary: A free condensed, bold Didone display serif inspired by a 1976 Greek book cover, with a sans companion.
description: Marx is a condensed and bold modern Didone serif with exceptional detail, ideal for display applications at large sizes, inspired by a 1976 book cover for a Greek translation of a work on Marxist sociology. It comes in a serif and a sans-serif variation.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Marx as a condensed and bold modern didone serif typeface with exceptional details, ideal for display applications in large text sizes, inspired by a 1976 book cover design.

name: Cornelius
classification_notes: A caps-and-small-caps Art Deco face copied from a metal sign, offered in clean and rough variants.
summary: A free caps-and-small-caps Art Deco display face copied from a Volos, Greece metal sign.
description: Cornelius is a caps and small-caps only typeface inspired by Italian Art Deco, based on the design found on a metal sign at the General Chemical State Laboratory in Volos, Greece. It ships free as a four-font pack, with clean and rough versions plus stylistic alternates.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Cornelius as a caps and small-caps only typeface inspired by Italian Art Deco, based on the design found on a metal sign on the General Chemical State Laboratory in Volos, Greece.

name: Walter
classification_notes: A bold, high-contrast stencil display face copied from a hand-painted army-camp sign, with hollow, layered and hand-drawn companions.
summary: A free, high-contrast stencil display face inspired by a hand-painted sign in a Greek army camp, with hollow and layered companions.
description: Walter is inspired by a hand-painted sign found in an old army camp in Evros, Northern Greece, emphasising high-contrast boldness. The free 16-font Walter Pack includes stencil, hollow and layered versions with hand-drawn variants, plus star, X, dot and diamond pattern fills.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Walter as inspired by a hand-painted sign found in an old army camp in Evros, Northern Greece, emphasising high contrast boldness across stencil, hollow, layered and hand-drawn variants.

name: Dönmeh
classification_notes: A caps-only display face with reversed stress copied from 1950s-60s Greek advertisements, its heavy horizontal strokes nodding to Arabic and Hebrew letterforms.
summary: A free caps-only display face with reversed stress, inspired by mid-century Greek sign painters and named for Thessaloniki's Dönmeh community.
description: Dönmeh is inspired by Greek advertisements from the 1950s and 60s using reversed stress, an unorthodox but popular approach among Greek sign painters, with heavy horizontal strokes nodding to Arabic and Hebrew letterforms. Named after a historical group of crypto-Jews in the Ottoman Empire, it is offered free with a request to donate to those in need.
foundry_blurb: Atypical describe Dönmeh as inspired by Greek advertisements from the 1950s-60s featuring reversed stress, a rather unorthodox but popular approach with Greek sign painters, released as a tribute to Thessaloniki's openness and cultural diversity.
